item.title: Before the Dawn in America’s Heartland
item.summary: With hardly a cloud in sight, astronauts had a sweeping view of nighttime lights in the U.S. Midwest.
item.page_text:
With hardly a cloud in sight, astronauts had a sweeping view of nighttime lights in the U.S. Midwest.
The predawn hours brought clear skies over much of the eastern United States on October 18, 2026. An astronaut aboard the International Space Station seized the opportunity to capture this wide-angle photo at 4:54 a.m. Central Daylight Time (09:54 Universal Time), with illuminated cities large and small arrayed across the darkened landscape.
The U.S. Midwest’s largest metropolitan areas , such as Chicago, Illinois, and Detroit, Michigan, stand out as some of the brightest features. Mid-sized cities—including Indianapolis, Indiana; Cincinnati, Ohio; and Louisville, Kentucky—and their interconnections along state and interstate highways also shine brightly.
Above the web of nighttime lights and Earth’s lower atmosphere, a diffuse layer of green and orange is visible along the horizon to the left. This band of light is airglow , produced when sunlight strikes atoms and molecules in the upper atmosphere and causes them to eject photons . To the right, light from the Sun arcs across the horizon; sunrise was about an hour away on the East Coast and about two hours away in Chicago.
Astronaut photos and other remote sensing observations of nighttime lights are scientifically valuable for tracking changes in the built environment. For example, Chicago's lightscape appears a homogeneous pale yellow in the wide view above. But in detailed photos, like the one below, a range of colors stemming from different types of lighting is discernible. Using NASA’s extensive Gateway to Astronaut Photography of Earth archive, researchers have developed a method for distinguishing lighting types within the pixels of nighttime photos. Systematically quantifying urban lights’ brightness, color, and extent can provide insight into how cities grow and evolve .
Satellite sensors also observe changes to lighting. In particular, NASA’s Black Marble nighttime lights product suite uses satellite observations to produce science-quality records of nighttime lights across the globe at daily, monthly, and yearly time scales. In the eastern U.S., scientists have used these data to track everything from power outages and restoration following major storms to lighting changes associated with new infrastructure to transitions to LED lighting from older forms.
Astronaut photograph ISS075-E-226709 was acquired on October 18, 2026, with a Nikon Z9 digital camera using a focal length of 14 millimeters, and photograph ISS070-E-105097 was acquired on March 1, 2024, with a Nikon D5 digital camera using a focal length of 400 millimeters. They are provided by the ISS Crew Earth Observations Facility and the Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit at NASA Johnson Space Center. The images were taken by members of the Expedition 75 and Expedition 70 crews, respectively. The images have been cropped and enhanced to improve contrast, and lens artifacts have been removed. The International Space Station Program supports the laboratory as part of the ISS National Lab to help astronauts take pictures of Earth that will be of the greatest value to scientists and the public, and to make those images freely available on the internet. Additional images taken by astronauts and cosmonauts can be viewed at the NASA/JSC Gateway to Astronaut Photography of Earth . Story by Lindsey Doermann.

item.page_text:
By clicking Continue to join or sign in, you agree to LinkedIn’s User Agreement , Privacy Policy , and Cookie Policy .
Can you Thanos-snap away the parts of a 3D Gaussian splat you don't want? Yeah, you can.
⠀
Here it's a splat of Microsoft's Redmond campus in CesiumJS, edited one typed sentence at a time. Nothing in the scene is labeled. Every Gaussian holds its own 1536-D embedding, built from what a vision model saw in 429 rendered views. A text query is matched against all of them, so any phrase becomes a selection.
⠀
A planner turns each sentence into tool calls that run per Gaussian in the shader: glow, spin, launch, dissolve.
⠀
Made with CesiumJS, Cesium ion, C-RADIOv4 ( NVIDIA ), SigLIP 2 ( Google DeepMind ), RADSeg and Anthropic Claude Code.
⠀ #GaussianSplatting #CesiumJS #GeospatialAI #ComputerVision
Would be super cool to see this applied as a VFX!
My goodness. I never stop being shocked by this kind of black magic.

item.title: #remotesensing #sentinel2 # geoai #climatetrace #methane #earthobservation | Ashutosh Pawar
item.summary: ... geospatial foundation model . We tested it across 5 countries with 3675 ... GeoAI #ClimateTRACE #Methane #EarthObservation.
item.page_text:
By clicking Continue to join or sign in, you agree to LinkedIn’s User Agreement , Privacy Policy , and Cookie Policy .
When I started learning remote sensing, I was amazed that a ratio of two or three spectral bands could reveal so much about vegetation, soil, and water. I never thought I’d get to build an index of my own. 🌎 🛰️

My first dissertation chapter is now out, open access in the International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation!

We introduce the Bovine Slurry Index (BSI), a Sentinel-2 index that maps liquid manure ponds within cattle operations identified by a geospatial foundation model. We tested it across 5 countries with 3,675 manure ponds. BSI outperformed standard water indices in every region, reaching up to 91% precision in the U.S.

Why it matters: manure ponds are a major source of livestock methane, and knowing where they are is a first step toward better emissions inventories.

Built with an amazing team: my advisor, Dr. Vasit Sagan , and my co-authors Derek Tesser , Alessandro Farbo, PhD , Edward Boyda, and Aaron Davitt , with support from the Remote Sensing Lab at Saint Louis University , Climate TRACE , and Earth Genome .

📄 Read it for free: https://lnkd.in/gR4ADg4g #RemoteSensing #Sentinel2 #GeoAI #ClimateTRACE #Methane #EarthObservation
Looks amazing!! I have been working in methane generation lab tests and geospatial data by separate, and I have never thought how both worlds could be merged, despite just simple gis processing. Congratulations!

A satellite image shows Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. American strikes targeting the Iranian island were reported Monday, the eve of midterm elections in the U.S.  (European Space Agency/Wikimedia Commons)
The U.S. struck an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz on the eve of Election Day, the latest in a series of what officials call limited defensive strikes against the country in recent weeks.
The strikes Monday targeting Qeshm Island came as President Donald Trump has talked up a diplomatic off-ramp to the Iran war. But Trump has been considering stepping up the conflict after Tuesday’s midterm elections, according to news reports.
Trump told Fox News on Tuesday morning that it was a “minor attack, it wasn’t a war,” and that it targeted an anti-aircraft facility that took Iran about two months to build.
“We watched it get built,” he said . “As soon as it was completed — we hit it.”
On Monday, he downplayed the prospect of a return to major fighting, posting on Truth Social that oil prices were falling and that Tehran wanted a settlement as soon as possible.
In remarks on the last day of campaigning before the midterm elections, Trump said “we haven’t been doing any fighting for months.”
But overnight, a series of blasts in rapid succession were heard on Qeshm Island, Al Jazeera reported , citing Iran’s state-owned IRNA news agency. Witnesses said they saw two planes flying over the island off Iran’s southern coast.
Oil is seen on the shoreline of Iran’s Qeshm Island on Aug. 13, 2026. The U.S. carried out strikes Monday on the island, a key point in the Strait of Hormuz. (Amirhosein Khorgooi/AP)
The largest island in the Persian Gulf, it is key terrain in Iran’s attempts to control shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global energy supplies.
At least two incidents Monday prompted U.S. strikes in the area, The Wall Street Journal reported , citing unidentified U.S. officials. CNN also reported details of one of the incidents, citing an unidentified official.
In that case, a U.S. fighter jet struck back in self-defense after Iran’s Revolutionary Guard fired a surface-to-air missile at it, the officials said.
In a separate instance, U.S. forces intercepted an Iranian missile fired the same day from Qeshm and targeting commercial shipping, one official told the newspaper.
U.S. Central Command often issues statements about its defensive strikes and sometimes provides video footage. It did not do either in these two cases.
The strikes Monday were part of a series of smaller-scale assaults in recent weeks that the U.S. sought to keep quiet to avoid indicating that major combat operations were resuming, officials told CNN and The Wall Street Journal.
CENTCOM did not immediately respond to questions about the strikes.
In recent days, reports have suggested Trump was mulling a strike hundreds of miles to the north on Pickaxe Mountain near Natanz, which houses a nuclear complex deep inside that Israel believes may hold stores of enriched uranium and the equipment Iran uses to make nuclear fuel.
In a Fox News appearance that aired Monday night, Trump said it would be “not a big deal” to hit the site.
“We can do it in literally, we can do that in one hour,” he said. “As soon as we want, at any time we want.”
Last week, CENTCOM boss Adm. Brad Cooper visited the White House to brief the president on military options in the conflict, The Wall Street Journal reported .
In a call with Axios on Monday, Trump said he was in “no rush” to resume strikes. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, CIA Director John Ratcliffe and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were advising him to let an economic pressure campaign play out instead, Axios reported.
Meanwhile, Iran has promised to respond to any escalation in the war with a harder and broader response that would not be confined to the Middle East.
Chad Garland is a Marine Corps veteran who covers the U.S. military in Vicenza, Italy, for Stars and Stripes. He previously covered military operations downrange in the Middle East and elsewhere. He has also reported for news outlets in Washington, D.C., Arizona, Oregon and California.

item.title: Russia unleashes massive assault on Ukrainian infrastructure in overnight blitz - NY Post
item.summary: Satellite imagery shows the aftermath of an attack on the Novokuybyshevsk refinery in Russia. 4. A satellite image shows the aftermath of Ukrainian ...
item.page_text:
Russia on Tuesday launched one of its biggest ever attacks on Ukraine’s infrastructure, forcing emergency power outages in multiple regions — while also disrupting the water supply to millions of civilians.
It came as rescuers in the south of the country continued their intense search for survivors at a bombed-out aid facility and shelter where at least 31 people were killed and dozens remain missing.
Ukraine’s national energy company said Russia had deliberately attacked its energy facilities more than 20 times, leading to the forcible application of emergency power outages in seven regions, including the capital, Kyiv, the outlet Ukrainska Pravda reported .
In regions where emergency outages weren’t in place, scheduled power cuts were applied on Tuesday, leaving some consumers without electricity for over 12 hours, the first such outages this fall.
Special emergency power outage schedules were implemented in Sumy and Poltava regions, with no indication as to when the outages might end.
Russia also hit a substation critical to the Khmelnytskyi Nuclear Power Plant, as it targeted transmission systems and power plants across the country, Ukraine’s energy minister, Denys Shmyhal, said on Tuesday, according to the Kyiv Independent .
“Such actions pose a threat not only to Ukraine but also to the nuclear safety of all of Europe,” Shmyhal said.
The minister has spoken to the International Atomic Energy Agency about the incident, while calling on Ukraine’s international partners to respond to the attack.
Major water supply facilities have been left without power, causing interruptions to Kyiv’s water supply.
“Thousands of power engineers have been working since the very night to deal with the aftermath of the attacks and restore the power supply. Critical infrastructure facilities will be reconnected first,” Ukrenergo, Ukraine’s energy supplier, said in a statement.
In total, Russia on Tuesday attacked Ukraine with 289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles, and 59 cruise missiles, Shmyhal said.
Ukraine’s largest private energy firm, DTEK, reported one of the “most serious attacks ever” on its facilities, halting production at three of its thermal power plants and damaging grid infrastructure in Odesa, according to CEO Maxim Timchenko.
“It is clear Russia is dangerously escalating its efforts to deny Ukrainians critical services like energy this winter. We will not let them succeed,” Timchenko said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s government is bracing for another energy crisis this winter, following last year’s Russian attacks, which saw millions of people without heating and power amid subzero temperatures.
“The Russians think America won’t notice this signal of theirs,” he said on social media. “But we need to notice and stop such terror. We need to help Ukraine defend its skies; otherwise, Russia will never stop its missile strikes.”
The latest attacks come as rescuers in the southern Zaporizhzhia region continued their work at the site of a Russian bombing at an aid facility and shelter in a school .
At least 31 people have been killed, and more than 45 are still missing at the site in the village of Komyshukakha, where Russia used nearly 1.5 tons of bunker-busting bombs in Monday’s attack.
“The scale of the tragedy is terrifying,” Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of the region’s military administration, wrote online.

“This is one of the worst tragedies in terms of the number of civilian victims in our region since the start of the full-scale war,” he added.
Zelensky on Tuesday traveled to Germany for the start of a new round of discussions with European leaders, ahead of next week’s US-brokered peace talks in Abu Dhabi.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed Tuesday that a Russian delegation will attend the talks, the first since February , aimed at ending the four-and-a-half-year war.

November Mapping Challenge, day 3: polygons.

- Neighbourhood boundaries: "Administrative units of the city of Barcelona", Open Data BCN portal (CC BY 4.0).
